description:
The outbound transfer arc drawn on the /fly screen has correct endpoints (Earth at dep_day, destination at arr_day) but the mid-point bulge is always the pure Hohmann ellipse regardless of the mission's actual arrival V∞. The V∞ value is read at the caller site (fly/+page.svelte:687) and passed to buildArcs, but buildArcs marks it as `_arrivalVInfKms` (intentionally unused) and calls transferEllipse(earthDep, destArr, ARC_STEPS) — which has no V∞ parameter and no shaping logic.

Expected: The outbound arc should bend in response to the mission's arrival V∞, matching the same V∞-shaping behaviour already present in outboundArc (src/lib/mission-arc.ts:78). Missions with V∞ above the Hohmann baseline (~2.94 km/s for Mars) should bulge outward; missions with V∞ below should bend inward. Endpoint pinning must be preserved.

Acceptance criteria:
- A mission with flight.arrival.v_infinity_km_s that differs from the Hohmann baseline must produce an outbound arc whose mid-point radial distance differs measurably from the pure two-focus ellipse — higher V∞ bends outward, lower V∞ bends inward. [reporter: Q: 'The bend direction and amount for the middle of the arc is determined by the mission's arrival V-infinity data... high V∞ visibly bends the middle away from it while both endpoints stay pinned']
- A mission with V∞ at the Hohmann baseline value must produce an arc that closely matches the pure Hohmann ellipse (mid-point radius within ~0.05 AU of a*(1-e²) for Mars). [reporter: Q: 'zero/low V∞ leaves the arc close to the baseline ellipse']
- The outbound arc endpoints must land exactly on the live Earth position (at dep_day) and the live destination position (at arr_day) — endpoint pinning must not be degraded by V∞ shaping. [reporter: Q: 'both endpoints stay pinned' and report: 'the endpoints are in the right places']
- Extremely high V∞ must not produce a numerically unstable, looping, or self-intersecting arc — the eccentricity bend must be clamped to a safe bound (matching the outboundArc guard: Math.max(-0.4, Math.min(0.6, ratio - 1)) * 0.12). [repo-data: src/lib/mission-arc.ts:128-129 — outboundArc already clamps this way]
- The /fly arc for any mission must match the /explore arc for the same mission parameters (same departure date, destination, V∞) within V∞-shaping tolerance, acknowledging that /explore uses outboundArc (single-endpoint pinning) while /fly uses transferEllipse (dual-endpoint pinning). [repo-data: static/data/missions/*.json: every heliocentric mission carries flight.arrival.v_infinity_km_s; both screens use the same mission data; src/lib/mission-arc.ts:78 vs :144 define two different arc builders from the same module]

Domain facts:
- Hohmann baseline V∞ for Mars ≈ 2.94 km/s (computed by outboundArc at mission-arc.ts:107-112 using µ_Sun = 4π² AU³/yr², AUPYR_TO_KMS = 4.7404)
- outboundArc uses signed eccentricity V∞ shaping: eSigned += Math.sign(eSigned || 1) * Math.max(-0.4, Math.min(0.6, ratio-1)) * 0.12
- transferEllipse uses two-focus geometry (circles at rA=2a-r1, rB=2a-r2) — no V∞ dimension exists in its parameter list
- The Hohmann baseline computation differs slightly between the two functions: outboundArc uses destA (circular orbital radius of destination) while transferEllipse uses live r2 (actual position radius); both converge for near-circular orbits

Target: src/lib/mission-arc.ts — transferEllipse
Do NOT change src/routes/fly/+page.svelte — already touched by the failed attempt (40 turns, 671s). The V∞ data arrives there but `buildArcs` drops it on the floor. Any re-attempt starting in fly/+page.svelte is a repeat of known-failed path. The computation owner is transferEllipse in mission-arc.ts; buildArcs just needs the underscore prefix removed and the V∞ threaded through. — it is not the owner of this symptom.
